+def _fill_missing_variables(datasets, dim, concat_over, variables_to_merge,
+                            dim_coords, dims_sizes, concat_dim_lengths, fill_value):
+    """
+    Fill in missing variables in datasets with NaN values.
+    
+    This allows concatenating datasets with different variables by filling
+    missing variables with NaN, similar to pandas.concat with outer join.
+    
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    datasets : list of Dataset
+        The datasets to fill
+    dim : str
+        The concatenation dimension name
+    concat_over : set
+        Variables to concatenate
+    variables_to_merge : set
+        Variables to merge
+    dim_coords : dict
+        Dimension coordinates
+    dims_sizes : dict
+        Dimension sizes
+    concat_dim_lengths : list
+        Length of each dataset along the concat dimension
+    fill_value : scalar
+        Value to use for filling missing data
+    """
+    from .variable import Variable
+    
+    # Collect all variables that need to be filled
+    all_vars = concat_over | variables_to_merge
+    
+    # For each dataset, fill in missing variables
+    for ds_idx, ds in enumerate(datasets):
+        missing_vars = all_vars - set(ds.variables)
+        
+        for var_name in missing_vars:
+            # Find a dataset that has this variable to get its metadata
+            ref_var = None
+            for other_ds in datasets:
+                if var_name in other_ds.variables:
+                    ref_var = other_ds.variables[var_name]
+                    break
+            
+            if ref_var is None:
+                continue
+            
+            # Determine the shape for the filled variable
+            fill_shape = []
+            for dim_name in ref_var.dims:
+                if dim_name == dim:
+                    # For the concat dimension, use the length for this dataset
+                    fill_shape.append(concat_dim_lengths[ds_idx])
+                else:
+                    # For other dimensions, use dims_sizes
+                    fill_shape.append(dims_sizes.get(dim_name, ref_var.shape[ref_var.dims.index(dim_name)]))
+            
+            fill_shape = tuple(fill_shape)
+            
+            # Create a NaN-filled array with the same dtype as the reference variable
+            # Use fill_value if provided, otherwise use NaN
+            if fill_value is dtypes.NA:
+                # Use NaN for floating point types, 0 for integer types
+                if np.issubdtype(ref_var.dtype, np.floating):
+                    filled_data = np.full(fill_shape, np.nan, dtype=ref_var.dtype)
+                else:
+                    filled_data = np.full(fill_shape, 0, dtype=ref_var.dtype)
+            else:
+                filled_data = np.full(fill_shape, fill_value, dtype=ref_var.dtype)
+            
+            # Add the filled variable to the dataset
+            ds.variables[var_name] = Variable(ref_var.dims, filled_data, ref_var.attrs)
+
